criteria.q1036: Vertical Velocity: The rate at which a body moves upwards at an angle of 90 degrees to the ground.
criteria.q1037: Vibrational Density of States: "Density of States" is the number of vibrational modes in an infinitesimal interval of angular frequency divided by the range of that interval and by volume.
criteria.q1038: Video Frame Rate: Frame rate (also known as frame frequency) is the frequency (rate) at which an imaging device produces unique consecutive images called frames.
criteria.q1039: Viscosity: Viscosity is a measure of the resistance of a fluid which is being deformed by either shear stress or extensional stress.
criteria.q1040: Visible Radiant Energy: "Visible Radiant Energy", also known as luminous energy, is the energy of electromagnetic waves.
criteria.q1041: Vision Thresholds: "Vision Thresholds" is the thresholds of sensitivity of the eye.
criteria.q1042: Voltage: $\textit{Voltage}$, also referred to as $\textit{Electric Tension}$, is the difference between electrical potentials of two points.
criteria.q1043: Voltage Imbalance: Voltage imbalance is the percentage deviation of individual phase voltages from the average voltage across phases in a polyphase electrical system.
criteria.q1044: Voltage Phasor: "Voltage Phasor" is a representation of voltage as a sinusoidal integral quantity using a complex quantity whose argument is equal to the initial phase and whose modulus is equal to the root-mean-square value.
criteria.q1046: Volume: The volume of a solid object is the three-dimensional concept of how much space it occupies, often quantified numerically.
criteria.q1047: Volume Flow Rate: Volumetric Flow Rate, (also known as volume flow rate, rate of fluid flow or volume velocity) is the volume of fluid which passes through a given surface per unit time.
criteria.q1048: Surface Related Volume Flow Rate: Surface Related Volume Flow Rate
criteria.q1049: Volume Flow Ratio: Volume flow ratio is commonly used in fluid dynamics and engineering, referring to the ratio of the flow rates of two or more fluid streams within a system.
criteria.q1050: Volume Fraction: "Volume Fraction" is the volume of a constituent divided by the volume of all constituents of the mixture prior to mixing.
criteria.q1051: Volume per Unit Area: Volume per Unit Area
criteria.q1052: Volume per Time: Volume per Time
criteria.q1053: Volume Strain: Volume, or volumetric, Strain, or dilatation (the relative variation of the volume) is the trace of the tensor $\vartheta$.
criteria.q1054: Volume Thermal Expansion: When the temperature of a substance changes, the energy that is stored in the intermolecular bonds between atoms changes.
criteria.q1055: Volumic Bit Density: Volumic Bit Density
criteria.q1056: Volumic Electric Charge: Volumic Electric Charge
criteria.q1057: Volumetric Flux: In fluid dynamics, the volumetric flux is the rate of volume flow across a unit area (m3·s−1·m−2).[Wikipedia]
criteria.q1058: Volumetric Heat Capacity: $\textit{Volumetric Heat Capacity (VHC)}$, also termed $\textit{volume-specific heat capacity}$, describes the ability of a given volume of a substance to store internal energy while undergoing a given temperature change, but without underg
criteria.q1059: Volumic Output Power: Volumic Output Power
criteria.q1060: Volumic Electromagnetic Energy: $\textit{Volumic Electromagnetic Energy}$, also known as the $\textit{Electromagnetic Energy Density}$, is the energy associated with an electromagnetic field, per unit volume of the field.
criteria.q1061: Vorticity: In the simplest sense, vorticity is the tendency for elements of a fluid to "spin." More formally, vorticity can be related to the amount of "circulation" or "rotation" (or more strictly, the local angular rate of rotation) in a fluid.
criteria.q1062: Warm Receptor Threshold: "Warm Receptor Threshold" is the threshold of warm-sensitive free nerve-ending.
criteria.q1063: Warping Constant: The "Warping Constant" is a measure for the warping constant or warping resistance of a cross section under torsional loading.
criteria.q1064: Warping Moment: The warping moment measure is a measure for the warping moment, which occurs in warping torsional analysis.
criteria.q1065: Water Horsepower: No pump can convert all of its mechanical power into water power.
criteria.q1066: Water Solubility: An amount of substance per unit volume that is the concentration of a saturated solution expressed as the ratio of the solute concentration over the volume of water.
criteria.q1067: Water vapour diffusion coefficient: The Water vapour diffusion coefficient describes how easy vapour diffusion happens in a given material.
criteria.q1068: Water Vapour Diffusion Coefficient: The Water vapour diffusion coefficient describes how easy vapour diffusion happens in a given material.
criteria.q1069: Wavelength: For a monochromatic wave, "wavelength" is the distance between two successive points in a direction perpendicular to the wavefront where at a given instant the phase differs by $2\pi$.
criteria.q1070: Wavenumber: "Wavenumber" is the spatial frequency of a wave - the number of waves that exist over a specified distance.
criteria.q1072: Web Time Average Pressure: Web Time Average Pressure
criteria.q1073: Web Time Average Thrust: Web Time Average Thrust
criteria.q1074: Weight: The force with which a body is attracted toward an astronomical body.
criteria.q1075: Wet Bulb Temperature: the temperature of a parcel of air cooled to saturation (100% relative humidity) by the evaporation of water into it, with the latent heat supplied by the parcel.
criteria.q1076: Width: "Width" is the middle of three dimensions: length, width, thickness.
criteria.q1077: Work: A force is said to do Work when it acts on a body so that there is a displacement of the point of application, however small, in the direction of the force.
criteria.q1078: Work Function: "Work Function" is the energy difference between an electron at rest at infinity and an electron at a certain energy level.
criteria.q1079: Zenith Angle: Zenith angle is the angle measured from the zenith (the point directly overhead) downward to a celestial object or direction of interest.

criteria.q497: Liquid Level: Liquid level refers to the measurement of the height of a liquid within a container.
criteria.q498: Liquid Volume: Liquid volume is the volume of a given amount of liquid, that is, the amount of space a liquid takes up.

criteria.q500: Logarithmic Ratio to Base 10: The common (base-10) logarithm of the ratio between the value of a defined quantity and the value of a reference quantity of the same type.

criteria.q502: Logarithmic Frequency Interval to Base 2: Logarithmic Frequency Interval to Base 2

criteria.q529: Moment of Inertia in the Z axis: The rotational inertia or resistance to change in direction or speed of rotation about a defined axis.
criteria.q530: Mach Number: "Mach Number" is a dimensionless quantity representing the speed of an object moving through air or other fluid divided by the local speed of sound.

criteria.q532: Macroscopic Total Cross-section: "Macroscopic Total Cross-section" is the total cross-sections for all atoms or other entities in a given 3D domain, divided by the volume of that domain.

criteria.q570: Mass Fraction of Water: Mass Fraction of Water is one of a number of Concentration quantities defined by ISO 80000.

criteria.q838: Section Modulus: The Section Modulus is a geometric property for a given cross-section used in the design of beams or flexural members.
criteria.q839: Seebeck Coefficient: "Seebeck Coefficient", or thermopower, or thermoelectric power of a material is a measure of the magnitude of an induced thermoelectric voltage in response to a temperature difference across that material.

criteria.q842: Service Factor: The value indicates the multiplier of the rated power that equipment can handle for some period of time when operating according to a manufacturer's specified conditions; typically applicable to motors.
criteria.q843: Shannon Diversity Index: Information entropy applied to a collection of indiviual organisms [of selected species] in a sample area.
criteria.q844: Shear Modulus: The Shear Modulus or modulus of rigidity, denoted by $G$, or sometimes $S$ or $\mu$, is defined as the ratio of shear stress to the shear strain.
criteria.q845: Shear Strain: Shear Strain is the amount of deformation perpendicular to a given line rather than parallel to it.
criteria.q846: Shear Stress: Shear stress occurs when the force occurs in shear, or perpendicular to the normal.

criteria.q849: Signal Detection Threshold: "Signal Detection Threshold" is a dimensionless measure of the threshold for detecting a signal against a background of noise.
criteria.q850: Signal Strength: In telecommunications, particularly in radio, signal strength refers to the magnitude of the electric field at a reference point that is a significant distance from the transmitting antenna.
criteria.q851: Slowing-Down Area: "Slowing-Down Area" in an infinite homogenous medium, is one-sixth of the mean square distance between the neutron source and the point where a neutron reaches a given energy.
criteria.q852: Slowing-Down Density: "Slowing-Down Density" is a measure of the rate at which neutrons lose energy in a nuclear reactor through collisions; equal to the number of neutrons that fall below a given energy per unit volume per unit time.
criteria.q853: Slowing-Down Length: "Slowing-Down Length" is the average straight-line distance that a fast neutron will travel between its introduction into the slowing-downmedium (moderator) and thermalization.
criteria.q854: Slowing-Down Area: "Slowing-Down Area" in an infinite homogenous medium, is one-sixth of the mean square distance between the neutron source and the point where a neutron reaches a given energy.
criteria.q855: Slowing-Down Density: "Slowing-Down Density" is a measure of the rate at which neutrons lose energy in a nuclear reactor through collisions; equal to the number of neutrons that fall below a given energy per unit volume per unit time.
criteria.q856: Slowing-Down Length: "Slowing-Down Length" is the average straight-line distance that a fast neutron will travel between its introduction into the slowing-downmedium (moderator) and thermalization.
criteria.q857: Soil Adsorption Coefficient: A specific volume that is the ratio of the amount of substance adsorbed per unit weight of organic carbon in the soil or sediment to the concentration of the chemical in aqueous solution at equilibrium.
criteria.q858: Solid Angle: The solid angle subtended by a surface S is defined as the surface area of a unit sphere covered by the surface S's projection onto the sphere.
criteria.q859: Diffusion Length (Solid State Physics): "Solid State Diffusion Length" is the average distance traveled by a particle, such as a minority carrier in a semiconductor
criteria.q860: Water Solubility: An amount of substance per unit volume that is the concentration of a saturated solution expressed as the ratio of the solute concentration over the volume of water.
criteria.q861: Sound Energy Density: Sound energy density is the time-averaged sound energy in a given volume divided by that volume.
criteria.q862: Sound Exposure: Sound Exposure is the energy of the A-weighted sound calculated over the measurement time(s).
criteria.q863: Sound Exposure Level: Sound Exposure Level abbreviated as $SEL$ and $LAE$, is the total noise energy produced from a single noise event, expressed as a logarithmic ratio from a reference level.
criteria.q864: Sound Intensity: Sound intensity or acoustic intensity ($I$) is defined as the sound power $P_a$ per unit area $A$.
criteria.q865: Sound Particle Acceleration: In a compressible sound transmission medium - mainly air - air particles get an accelerated motion: the particle acceleration or sound acceleration with the symbol a in $m/s2$.
criteria.q866: Sound Particle Displacement: Sound Particle Displacement is the nstantaneous displacement of a particle in a medium from what would be its position in the absence of sound waves.
criteria.q867: Sound Particle Velocity: Sound Particle velocity is the velocity v of a particle (real or imagined) in a medium as it transmits a wave.
criteria.q868: Sound Power: Sound power or acoustic power $P_a$ is a measure of sonic energy $E$ per time $t$ unit.
criteria.q869: Sound Power Level: Sound Power Level abbreviated as $SWL$ expresses sound power more practically as a relation to the threshold of hearing - 1 picoW - in a logarithmic scale.
criteria.q870: Sound Pressure: Sound Pressure is the difference between instantaneous total pressure and static pressure.
criteria.q871: Sound Pressure Level: Sound pressure level ($SPL$) or sound level is a logarithmic measure of the effective sound pressure of a sound relative to a reference value.
criteria.q872: Sound Reduction Index: The Sound Reduction Index is used to measure the level of sound insulation provided by a structure such as a wall, window, door, or ventilator.
criteria.q873: Sound Volume Velocity: Sound Volume Velocity is the product of particle velocity $v$ and the surface area $S$ through which an acoustic wave of frequency $f$ propagates.
criteria.q874: Source Voltage: The quantity kind $\textit{Source Voltage}$, also referred to as $\textit{Source Tension}$ is the voltage between the two terminals of a voltage source when there is no electric current through the source.
criteria.q875: Source Voltage Between Substances: "Source Voltage Between Substances" is the source voltage between substance a and b.
criteria.q876: Spatial Summation Function: "Spatial Summation Function" is he ability to produce a composite signal from the signals coming into the eyes from different directions.
criteria.q877: Specific Acoustic Impedance: $\textit{Specific Acoustic Impedance}$ at a point in a medium is the complex quotient of the sound pressure $p$ by the particle velocity $v$ in the direction of wave propagation: $z = p / v$.
criteria.q878: Specific Activity: The "Specific Activity" is the number of decays per unit time of a radioactive sample.
criteria.q879: Specific Electric Charge: Electric charge (often capacity in the context of electrochemical cells) relativ to the mass (often only active components).
criteria.q880: Specific Electrical Current: "Specific Electric Current" is a measure to specify the applied current relative to a corresponding mass.
criteria.q881: Specific Energy: $\textit{Specific Energy}$ is defined as the energy per unit mass.
criteria.q882: Specific Energy Imparted: The "Specific Energy Imparted", is the energy imparted to an element of irradiated matter divided by the mass, dm, of that element.
criteria.q883: Specific Enthalpy: $\textit{Specific Enthalpy}$ is enthalpy per mass of substance involved.
criteria.q884: Specific Entropy: "Specific Entropy" is entropy per unit of mass.
criteria.q885: Specific Gibbs Energy: Energy has corresponding intensive (size-independent) properties for pure materials.
criteria.q886: Specific Heat Capacity: Specific Heat Capacity of a solid or liquid is defined as the heat required to raise unit mass of substance by one degree of temperature.
criteria.q887: Specific Heat Capacity at Constant Pressure: Specific heat at a constant pressure.
criteria.q888: Specific Heat Capacity at Constant Volume: Specific heat per constant volume.
criteria.q889: Specific Heat Capacity at Saturation: Specific heat per constant volume.
criteria.q890: Specific Heat Pressure: Specific heat at a constant pressure.
criteria.q891: Specific Heat Volume: Specific heat per constant volume.
criteria.q892: Specific Heats Ratio: The ratio of specific heats, for the exhaust gases adiabatic gas constant, is the relative amount of compression/expansion energy that goes into temperature $T$ versus pressure $P$ can be characterized by the heat capacity ratio: $\gamma\fr
criteria.q893: Specific Helmholtz Energy: $\textit{Specific Helmholtz Energy}$ is a "corresponding intensive property", which is $\textit{Helmholz Energy}$ per mass of substance involved.
criteria.q894: Specific Humidity: Specific humidity (or moisture content) is the ratio of the mass of water vapour to the total mass of the air parcel.
criteria.q895: Specific Impulse: The impulse produced by a rocket divided by the mass $mp$ of propellant consumed.

criteria.q896: Specific Impulse by Mass: Specific Impulse by Mass

criteria.q898: Specific Internal Energy: Energy has corresponding intensive (size-independent) properties for pure materials.
criteria.q899: Specific Modulus: Specific modulus is a materials property consisting of the elastic modulus per mass density of a material.
criteria.q900: Specific Optical Rotatory Power: The "Specific Optical Rotatory Power" Angle of optical rotation divided by the optical path length through the medium and by the mass concentration of the substance giving the specific optical rotatory power.
criteria.q901: Specific Power: Specific power, also known as power-to-weight ratio, is the amount of power output per unit mass of the power source.
criteria.q902: Specific Surface Area: Specific surface area (SSA) is a property of solids defined as the total surface area (SA) of a material per unit mass, (with units of m²/kg or m²/g).
criteria.q903: Specific Thrust: Specific impulse (usually abbreviated Isp) is a way to describe the efficiency of rocket and jet engines.
criteria.q904: Specific Volume: "Specific Volume" ($\nu$) is the volume occupied by a unit of mass of a material.
criteria.q905: Specific Weight: The specific weight, also known as the unit weight is a volume-specific quantity defined as the weight per unit volume of a material.
criteria.q906: Spectral Angular Cross-section: "Spectral Angular Cross-section" is the cross-section for ejecting or scattering a particle into an elementary cone with energy $E$ in an energy interval, divided by the solid angle $d\Omega$ of that cone and the range $dE$ of that interval
criteria.q907: Spectral Cross-section: "Spectral Cross-section" is the cross-section for a process in which the energy of the ejected or scattered particle is in an interval of energy, divided by the range $dE$ of this interval.
criteria.q908: Spectral Density of Vibrational Modes: The number of vibrational modes in an infinitesimal interval of angular frequency, divided by the size of that interval and by volume.
criteria.q909: Measurement Unit of Spectral Emittance: Spectral Emittance is a radiometry term for the power per unit area of electromagnetic radiation unit wavelength emerging from a surface.
criteria.q910: Measurement Unit of Spectral Irradiance: Spectral Irradiance is a radiometry term for the power per unit area of electromagnetic radiation per unit wavelength incident at a surface.
criteria.q911: Spectral Luminous Efficiency: The Spectral Luminous Efficiency is a measure of how well a light source produces visible light.
criteria.q912: Measurement Unit of Spectral Radiance: Spectral Radiance is a radiometry term for the power per unit area of electromagnetic radiation per unit wavelength per unit solid angle emerging from a surface.
criteria.q913: Spectral Radiant Energy Density: "Spectral Radiant Energy Density" is the spectral concentration of radiant energy density (in terms of wavelength), or the spectral radiant energy density (in terms of wave length).
criteria.q914: Spectral Radiant Energy Density in Terms of Wavelength: Spectral Radiant Energy Density in Terms of Wavelength
criteria.q915: Speed: Speed is the magnitude of velocity.
criteria.q916: Speed of Light: The quantity kind $\text{Speed of Light}$ is the speed of electomagnetic waves in a given medium.
criteria.q917: Speed of Sound: The speed of sound is the distance travelled during a unit of time by a sound wave propagating through an elastic medium.
criteria.q918: Speed Ratio: Speed ratio generally refers to the ratio of the rotational speeds of two interconnected rotating components, but it sometimes relates linear speeds.
criteria.q919: Illuminance: Spherical illuminance is equal to quotient of the total luminous flux $\Phi_v$ incident on a small sphere by the cross section area of that sphere.
criteria.q920: Spin: In quantum mechanics and particle physics "Spin" is an intrinsic form of angular momentum carried by elementary particles, composite particles (hadrons), and atomic nuclei.
criteria.q921: Spin Quantum Number: The "Spin Quantum Number" describes the spin (intrinsic angular momentum) of the electron within that orbital, and gives the projection of the spin angular momentum S along the specified axis
criteria.q924: Standard Absolute Activity: The "Standard Absolute Activity" is proportional to the absoulte activity of the pure substance $B$ at the same temperature and pressure multiplied by the standard pressure.
criteria.q925: Standard Chemical Potential: "Standard Chemical Potential" is the value of the chemical potential at standard conditions
criteria.q926: Standard Gravitational Parameter: In celestial mechanics the standard gravitational parameter of a celestial body is the product of the gravitational constant G and the mass M of the body.
criteria.q927: State Density as Expression of Angular Frequency: Quotient aus Anzahl von Vibrationsmodi in einem infinitesimalen Intervall der Kreisfrequenz durch die Spannweite dieses Intervalls und das Volumen
criteria.q928: State of Charge: ""State of Charge",quantifies the remaining capacity available in a battery at a given time and in relation to a given state of ageing.
criteria.q929: Static Friction: Static friction is friction between two or more solid objects that are not moving relative to each other.
criteria.q930: Static Friction Coefficient: Static friction is friction between two or more solid objects that are not moving relative to each other.
criteria.q931: Static Pressure: "Static Pressure" is the pressure at a nominated point in a fluid.
criteria.q932: Statistical Weight: A "Statistical Weight" is the relative probability (possibly unnormalized) of a particular feature of a state.
criteria.q933: Stochastic Process: In probability theory, a stochastic process, or sometimes random process is a collection of random variables; this is often used to represent the evolution of some random value, or system, over time.
criteria.q934: Stoichiometric Number: Chemical reactions, as macroscopic unit operations, consist of simply a very large number of elementary reactions, where a single molecule reacts with another molecule.
criteria.q935: Strain: In any branch of science dealing with materials and their behaviour, strain is the geometrical expression of deformation caused by the action of stress on a physical body.
criteria.q936: Strain Energy Density: Defined as the 'work done' for a given strain, that is the area under the stress-strain curve after a specified eation.
criteria.q937: Strain Energy Release Rate: In fracture mechanics, the energy release rate, G, is the rate at which energy is transformed as a material undergoes fracture.
criteria.q938: Stress: Stress is a measure of the average amount of force exerted per unit area of a surface within a deformable body on which internal forces act.
criteria.q939: Stress Intensity Factor: In fracture mechanics, the stress intensity factor (K) is used to predict the stress state ("stress intensity") near the tip of a crack or notch caused by a remote load or residual stresses.
criteria.q940: Stress-Optic Coefficient: When a ray of light passes through a photoelastic material, its electromagnetic wave components are resolved along the two principal stress directions and each component experiences a different refractive index due to the birefringence.
criteria.q941: Structural Efficiency: Structural efficiency is a function of the weight of structure to the afforded vehicle's strength.
criteria.q942: Structure Factor: "Structure Factor" is a mathematical description of how a material scatters incident radiation.
criteria.q943: Sun Protection Factor of a Product: Sun Protection Factor of a Product
criteria.q944: Superconduction Transition Temperature: "Superconduction Transition Temperature" is the critical thermodynamic temperature of a superconductor.
criteria.q945: Superconductor Energy Gap: "Superconductor Energy Gap" is the width of the forbidden energy band in a superconductor.
criteria.q946: Surface Activity Density: The "Surface Activity Density" is undefined.
criteria.q947: Surface Coefficient of Heat Transfer: Surface Coefficient of Heat Transfer
criteria.q948: Surface Density: The area density (also known as areal density, surface density, or superficial density) of a two-dimensional object is calculated as the mass per unit area.
criteria.q949: Surface‑related Volume Flow Rate: Surface‑related Volume Flow Rate
criteria.q950: Surface Tension: "Surface Tension" is a contractive tendency of the surface of a liquid that allows it to resist an external force.
criteria.q951: Susceptance: "Susceptance" is the imaginary part of admittance.
criteria.q952: Systolic Blood Pressure: The pressure of blood in the arteries which rises to a maximum as blood is pumped out by the left ventricle (systole) and drops to a minimum in diastole.
criteria.q953: Target Bogie Mass: An informal mass limit established by a Project Office (at the Element Integrated Product Team (IPT) level or below) to control mass.
criteria.q954: Temperature: Temperature is a physical property of matter that quantitatively expresses the common notions of hot and cold.
criteria.q955: Temperature Amount of Substance: Temperature Amount of Substance
criteria.q956: Temperature Difference: Temperature difference (Delta T) is the difference of temperatures between two measuring points
criteria.q957: Temperature Gradient: The temperature gradient measures the difference of a temperature per length, as for instance used in an external wall or its layers.
criteria.q958: Temperature per Magnetic Flux Density: Temperature per Magnetic Flux Density
criteria.q959: Temperature per Square Time: Temperature per Square Time

criteria.q969: Thermal Conductance: This quantity is also called "Heat Transfer Coefficient".
criteria.q970: Thermal Conductivity: In physics, thermal conductivity, $k$ (also denoted as $\lambda$), is the property of a material's ability to conduct heat.

criteria.q972: Thermal Diffusion Ratio: The "Thermal Diffusion Ratio" is proportional to the product of the component concentrations.
criteria.q973: Thermal Diffusion Coefficient: Thermal Diffusion Coefficient
criteria.q974: Thermal Diffusivity: In heat transfer analysis, thermal diffusivity (usually denoted $\alpha$ but $a$, $\kappa$,$k$, and $D$ are also used) is the thermal conductivity divided by density and specific heat capacity at constant pressure.
criteria.q975: Thermal Efficiency: Thermal efficiency is a dimensionless performance measure of a thermal device such as an internal combustion engine, a boiler, or a furnace.
criteria.q976: Thermal Energy: "Thermal Energy" is the portion of the thermodynamic or internal energy of a system that is responsible for the temperature of the system.
criteria.q977: Thermal Energy Length: Thermal Energy Length
criteria.q978: Thermal Expansion Coefficient: The "Thermal Expansion Coefficient" is a measure of the thermal expansion coefficient of a material, which expresses its elongation (as a ratio) per temperature difference.
criteria.q979: Measurement Unit of Thermal Inertia: Thermal inertia is a term used to describe the observed delays in a body's temperature response during heat transfers
criteria.q980: Thermal Insulance: $\textit{Thermal Insulance}$ is the reduction of heat transfer (the transfer of thermal energy between objects of differing temperature) between objects in thermal contact or in range of radiative influence.
criteria.q981: Thermal Power: Thermal power is the rate at which thermal energy is transferred or converted, expressed as energy per unit time.
criteria.q982: Thermal Resistance: $\textit{Thermal Resistance}$ is a heat property and a measure of a temperature difference by which an object or material resists a heat flow (heat per time unit or thermal resistance).
criteria.q983: Thermal Resistivity: The reciprocal of thermal conductivity is thermal resistivity, measured in $kelvin-metres$ per watt ($K \cdot m/W$).
criteria.q984: Thermal Transmittance: Thermal transmittance is the rate of transfer of heat through matter.
criteria.q985: Thermal Utilization Factor: The "Thermal Utilization Factor" in an infinite medium, is the ratio of the number of thermal absorbed in a fissionable nuclide or in a nuclear fuel, as specified, to the total number of thermal neutrons absorbed.
criteria.q986: Thermal Utilization Factor for Fission: Probability that a neutron that gets absorbed does so in the fuel material.
criteria.q987: Thermodynamic Critical Magnetic Flux Density: "Thermodynamic Critical Magnetic Flux Density" is the maximum magnetic field strength below which a material remains superconducting.
criteria.q989: Thermodynamic Entropy: Thermodynamic Entropy is a measure of the unavailability of a system’s energy to do work.
criteria.q990: Thermodynamic Temperature: Thermodynamic temperature is the absolute measure of temperature and is one of the principal parameters of thermodynamics.
criteria.q991: Thickness: "Thickness" is the the smallest of three dimensions: length, width, thickness.
criteria.q992: Thomson Coefficient: "Thomson Coefficient" represents Thomson heat power developed, divided by the electric current and the temperature difference.
criteria.q993: Thrust: Thrust is a reaction force described quantitatively by Newton's Second and Third Laws.
criteria.q994: Thrust Coefficient: The thrust force of a jet-propulsion engine per unit of frontal area per unit of incompressible dynamic pressure
criteria.q995: Thrust to Mass Ratio: Thrust to Mass Ratio
criteria.q996: Thrust to Weight Ratio: Thrust-to-weight ratio is a ratio of thrust to weight of a rocket, jet engine, propeller engine, or a vehicle propelled by such an engine.
criteria.q997: Tilt: The angle between an object's orientation vector relative to a reference frame.
criteria.q998: Time: Time is a basic component of the measuring system used to sequence events, to compare the durations of events and the intervals between them, and to quantify the motions of objects.
criteria.q999: Time Averaged Sound Intensity: Sound intensity or acoustic intensity ($I$) is defined as the sound power $P_a$ per unit area $A$.
criteria.q1000: time constant (inductance based): time constant (inductance based)
criteria.q1001: Time per Count: Time passed between N occurrences of a recurring phenomenon.
criteria.q1005: Torque: In physics, a torque ($\tau$) is a vector that measures the tendency of a force to rotate an object about some axis.
criteria.q1006: Torque per Angle: Torque per Angle
criteria.q1007: Torque per Length: Torque per Length
criteria.q1009: Torsional Spring Constant: Quotient Drehmoment zur elastischen Verformung einer Drehfeder durch den zugehörigen Drehwinkel
criteria.q1010: Total Angular Momentum: "Total Angular Momentum" combines both the spin and orbital angular momentum of all particles and fields.
criteria.q1011: Total Angular Momentum Quantum Number: The "Total Angular Quantum Number" describes the magnitude of total angular momentum $J$, where $j$ refers to a specific particle and $J$ is used for the whole system.

criteria.q1013: Total Cross-section: "Total Cross-section" is related to the absorbance of the light intensity through Beer-Lambert's law.
criteria.q1014: Total Current: "Total Current" is the sum of the electric current that is flowing through a surface and the displacement current.
criteria.q1015: Total Current Density: "Total Current Density" is the sum of the electric current density and the displacement current density.
criteria.q1016: Total Ionization: "Total Ionization" by a particle, total mean charge, divided by the elementary charge, $e$, of all positive ions produced by an ionizing charged particle along its entire path and along the paths of any secondary charged particles.
criteria.q1017: Total Linear Stopping Power: The "Total Linear Stopping Power" is defined as the average energy loss of the particle per unit path length.
criteria.q1018: Total Mass Stopping Power: If a substance is compared in gaseous and solid form, then the linear stopping powers of the two states are very different just because of the different density.
criteria.q1019: Total Pressure: The total pressure is the sum of the dynamic and static pressures, that is $P_0 = P + q$.
criteria.q1020: Touch Thresholds: "Touch Thresholds" is an umbrella term for the thresholds of sensitivity of the skin to touch, vibration and other mechanical stimuli.
criteria.q1021: Transmittance: Transmittance is the fraction of incident light (electromagnetic radiation) at a specified wavelength that passes through a sample.
criteria.q1022: Transmittance Density: Transmittance is the fraction of incident light (electromagnetic radiation) at a specified wavelength that passes through a sample.
criteria.q1023: Turbidity: Turbidity is the cloudiness or haziness of a fluid, or of air, caused by individual particles (suspended solids) that are generally invisible to the naked eye, similar to smoke in air.

criteria.q1029: Vapour Permeance: A material's "permeance", is dependent on thickness much like the R-value in heat transmission.

criteria.q1032: Vapour Permeance: A material's "permeance", is dependent on thickness much like the R-value in heat transmission.

criteria.q1034: Velocity: In kinematics, velocity is the speed of an object and a specification of its direction of motion.
criteria.q1035: Ventilation Rate per Floor Area: Ventilation Rate is often expressed by the volumetric flowrate of outdoor air introduced to a building.
criteria.q1036: Vertical Velocity: The rate at which a body moves upwards at an angle of 90 degrees to the ground.
criteria.q1037: Vibrational Density of States: "Density of States" is the number of vibrational modes in an infinitesimal interval of angular frequency divided by the range of that interval and by volume.
criteria.q1038: Video Frame Rate: Frame rate (also known as frame frequency) is the frequency (rate) at which an imaging device produces unique consecutive images called frames.
criteria.q1039: Viscosity: Viscosity is a measure of the resistance of a fluid which is being deformed by either shear stress or extensional stress.
criteria.q1040: Visible Radiant Energy: "Visible Radiant Energy", also known as luminous energy, is the energy of electromagnetic waves.
criteria.q1041: Vision Thresholds: "Vision Thresholds" is the thresholds of sensitivity of the eye.
criteria.q1042: Voltage: $\textit{Voltage}$, also referred to as $\textit{Electric Tension}$, is the difference between electrical potentials of two points.
criteria.q1043: Voltage Imbalance: Voltage imbalance is the percentage deviation of individual phase voltages from the average voltage across phases in a polyphase electrical system.
criteria.q1044: Voltage Phasor: "Voltage Phasor" is a representation of voltage as a sinusoidal integral quantity using a complex quantity whose argument is equal to the initial phase and whose modulus is equal to the root-mean-square value.
criteria.q1046: Volume: The volume of a solid object is the three-dimensional concept of how much space it occupies, often quantified numerically.
criteria.q1047: Volume Flow Rate: Volumetric Flow Rate, (also known as volume flow rate, rate of fluid flow or volume velocity) is the volume of fluid which passes through a given surface per unit time.
criteria.q1048: Surface Related Volume Flow Rate: Surface Related Volume Flow Rate
criteria.q1049: Volume Flow Ratio: Volume flow ratio is commonly used in fluid dynamics and engineering, referring to the ratio of the flow rates of two or more fluid streams within a system.
criteria.q1050: Volume Fraction: "Volume Fraction" is the volume of a constituent divided by the volume of all constituents of the mixture prior to mixing.
criteria.q1051: Volume per Unit Area: Volume per Unit Area
criteria.q1052: Volume per Time: Volume per Time
criteria.q1053: Volume Strain: Volume, or volumetric, Strain, or dilatation (the relative variation of the volume) is the trace of the tensor $\vartheta$.
criteria.q1054: Volume Thermal Expansion: When the temperature of a substance changes, the energy that is stored in the intermolecular bonds between atoms changes.
criteria.q1055: Volumic Bit Density: Volumic Bit Density

property.fullDefinition: For a monochromatic wave, "wavelength" is the distance between two successive points in a direction perpendicular to the wavefront where at a given instant the phase differs by $2\pi$. criteria.q547: Magnetic Tension: Magnetic Tension is a scalar quantity equal to the line integral of the magnetic field strength H along a specified path linking two points a and b.

criteria.q560: Mass Concentration of Water Vapour: Mass Concentration of Water is one of a number of Concentration quantities defined by ISO 80000.

criteria.q563: Mass Density: The mass density or density of a material is its mass per unit volume.
criteria.q564: Mass Energy Transfer Coefficient: "Mass Energy Transfer Coefficient" is that fraction of the mass attenuation coefficient which contributes to the production of kinetic energy in charged particles.
criteria.q565: Mass Equivalent: "Mass Equivalent" is the mass of a substance that reacts with (or is equivalent to) an arbitrary mass of another substance in a given chemical reaction.

criteria.q567: Mass Flow Rate: "Mass Flow Rate" is a measure of Mass flux.
criteria.q568: Mass Fraction: The "Mass Fraction" is the fraction of one substance with mass to the mass of the total mixture .
criteria.q569: Mass Fraction of Dry Matter: "Mass Fraction of Dry Matter" is one of a number of Concentration quantities defined by ISO 80000.
criteria.q570: Mass Fraction of Water: Mass Fraction of Water is one of a number of Concentration quantities defined by ISO 80000.
criteria.q571: Mass Number: The "Mass Number" (A), also called atomic mass number or nucleon number, is the total number of protons and neutrons (together known as nucleons) in an atomic nucleus.

criteria.q599: Mean Lifetime: The "Mean Lifetime" is the average length of time that an element remains in the set of discrete elements in a decaying quantity, $N(t)$.

criteria.q602: Mechanical Energy: Mechanical Energy is the sum of potential energy and kinetic energy.

criteria.q609: Migration Area: "Migration Area" is the sum of the slowing-down area from fission energy to thermal energy and the diffusion area for thermal neutrons.

criteria.q611: Mobility: "Mobility" characterizes how quickly a particle can move through a metal or semiconductor, when pulled by an electric field.

criteria.q613: Modulus of Admittance: "Modulus Of Admittance" is the absolute value of the quantity "admittance".
criteria.q614: Modulus of Elasticity: The Modulus of Elasticity is the mathematical description of an object or substance's tendency to be deformed elastically (that is, non-permanently) when a force is applied to it.

criteria.q617: Modulus of Rotational Subgrade Reaction: Modulus of Rotational Subgrade Reaction is a measure for modulus of rotational subgrade reaction, which expresses the rotational elastic bending of a linear structural element per length, such as for a beam.
criteria.q618: Modulus of Subgrade Reaction: Modulus of Subgrade Reaction is a geotechnical measure describing interaction between foundation structures and the soil.
criteria.q620: Molality of Solute: The "Molality of Solute" of a solution is defined as the amount of substance of solute divided by the mass in kg of the solvent.
criteria.q621: Molar Absorption Coefficient: "Molar Absorption Coefficient" is a spectrophotometric unit indicating the light a substance absorbs with respect to length, usually centimeters, and concentration, usually moles per liter.
criteria.q622: Molar Angular Momentum: Molar Angular Momentum
criteria.q623: Molar Attenuation Coefficient: "Molar Attenuation Coefficient" is a measurement of how strongly a chemical species or substance absorbs or scatters light at a given wavelength, per amount of substance.
criteria.q624: Molar Conductivity: "Molar Conductivity" is the conductivity of an electrolyte solution divided by the molar concentration of the electrolyte, and so measures the efficiency with which a given electrolyte conducts electricity in solution.
criteria.q625: Molar Energy: "Molar Energy" is the total energy contained by a thermodynamic system.
criteria.q626: Molar Entropy: The "Standard Molar Entropy" is the entropy content of one mole of substance, under standard conditions (not standard temperature and pressure STP).
criteria.q627: Molar Equivalent: "Molar Equivalent" is the amount of a substance that reacts with (or is equivalent to) an arbitrary amount (typically one mole) of another substance in a given chemical reaction.
criteria.q628: Molar Flow Rate: Molar Flow Rate is a measure of the amount of substance (the number of molecules) that passes through a given area perpendicular to the flow in a given time.
criteria.q629: Molar Flux Density: the rate at which moles of a substance pass through a unit area per unit time.

criteria.q633: Molar Internal Energy: Molar Internal Energy
criteria.q634: Molar Mass: In chemistry, the molar mass M is defined as the mass of a given substance (chemical element or chemical compound) divided by its amount of substance.
criteria.q635: Molar Optical Rotatory Power: The "Molar Optical Rotatory Power" Angle of optical rotation divided by the optical path length through the medium and by the amount concentration giving the molar optical rotatory power.
criteria.q636: Molar Refractivity: A quantity kind that is a measure of the total polarizability of a mole of substance that depends on the temperature, the index of refraction and the pressure.
criteria.q637: Molar Volume: The molar volume, symbol $V_m$, is the volume occupied by one mole of a substance (chemical element or chemical compound) at a given temperature and pressure.
criteria.q638: Mole Fraction: In chemistry, the mole fraction of a component in a mixture is the relative proportion of molecules belonging to the component to those in the mixture, by number of molecules.

state.task: Identify a scalar/ordered property whose comparison answers or explains this question. Candidate definitions describe properties, not facts about these particular entities.

g0.instructions: Select the most relevant ordered property in this set for comparing these entities in the user question. Prefer an actual property rather than the observed outcome itself.

criteria.q768: Radiant Energy: In radiometry,"Radiant Energy} is the energy of electromagnetic waves.
criteria.q769: Radiant Energy Density: "Radiant Energy Density", or radiant power, is the radiant energy per unit volume.
criteria.q770: Radiant Energy Exposure: Radiant Energy Exposure
criteria.q771: Radiant Exposure: Radiant exposure is a measure of the total radiant energy incident on a surface per unit area; equal to the integral over time of the radiant flux density.
criteria.q772: Radiant Fluence: Radiant fluence rate, or spherical irradiance, is equal to the total radiant flux incident on a small sphere divided by the area of the diametrical cross-section of the sphere.
criteria.q773: Radiant Fluence Rate: Radiant fluence rate, or spherical irradiance, is equal to the total radiant flux incident on a small sphere divided by the area of the diametrical cross-section of the sphere.
criteria.q774: Radiant Flux: Radiant Flux, or radiant power, is the measure of the total power of electromagnetic radiation (including infrared, ultraviolet, and visible light).
criteria.q775: Radiant Intensity: Radiant Intensity is a measure of the intensity of electromagnetic radiation.
criteria.q776: Radiative Heat Transfer: "Radiative Heat Transfer" is proportional to $(T_1^4 - T_2^4)$ and area of the surface, where $T_1$ and $T_2$ are thermodynamic temperatures of two black surfaces, for non totally black surfaces an additional factor less than 1 is needed.
criteria.q778: Radiosity: Radiosity is the total emitted and reflected radiation leaving a surface.
criteria.q779: Radius: In classical geometry, the "Radius" of a circle or sphere is any line segment from its center to its perimeter the radius of a circle or sphere is the length of any such segment.
criteria.q780: Radius of Curvature: In geometry, the "Radius of Curvature", R, of a curve at a point is a measure of the radius of the circular arc which best approximates the curve at that point.
criteria.q781: Radon Exposure: Radon Exposure is the integral with respect to time of radon activity concentration accumulated during the exposure time.
criteria.q782: Rate of Change: Rate of Change is a dimensionless change per unit time, such as a percentage change per second.
criteria.q783: Rate of Change of Frequency: The "Rate of Change of Frequency" is the rate of change of frequency with respect to time.
criteria.q784: Rate of Rise of Voltage: Rate of Rise of Voltage
criteria.q786: Ratio of Specific Heat Capacities: The specific heat ratio of a gas is the ratio of the specific heat at constant pressure, $c_p$, to the specific heat at constant volume, $c_V$.
criteria.q787: Reactance: "Reactance" is the opposition of a circuit element to a change of electric current or voltage, due to that element's inductance or capacitance.
criteria.q788: Reaction Energy: "Reaction Energy" in a nuclear reaction, is the sum of the kinetic energies and photon energies of the reaction products minus the sum of the kinetic and photon energies of the reactants.
criteria.q789: Reactive Charge: Reactive charge is the amount of chemical unit charge, positive or negative, that reactive species donate, accept, or exchange in a chemical process.
criteria.q790: Reactive Charge per Mass: Reactive Charge per Mass
criteria.q791: Reactive Energy: Reactive energy is the integral of reactive power over time, representing the energy exchanged between the source and reactive elements (inductors and capacitors) in an AC electrical circuit.
criteria.q792: Reactive Power: "Reactive Power", for a linear two-terminal element or two-terminal circuit, under sinusoidal conditions, is the quantity equal to the product of the apparent power $S$ and the sine of the displacement angle $\psi$.
criteria.q793: Reactivity: "Reactivity" characterizes the deflection of reactor from the critical state.
criteria.q794: Reactor Time Constant: The "Reactor Time Constant", also called the reactor period, is the time during which the neutron flux density in a reactor changes by the factor e = 2.718 (e: basis of natural logarithms), when the neutron flux density increases or decreas
criteria.q795: Recombination Coefficient: The "Recombination Coefficient" is the rate of recombination of positive ions with electrons or negative ions in a gas, per unit volume, divided by the product of the number of positive ions per unit volume and the number of electrons or ne
criteria.q796: Reflectance: Reflectance generally refers to the fraction of incident power that is reflected at an interface, while the term "reflection coefficient" is used for the fraction of electric field reflected.
criteria.q797: Reflectance Factor: Reflectance Factor is the measure of the ability of a surface to reflect light or other electromagnetic radiation, equal to the ratio of the reflected flux to the incident flux.
criteria.q798: Reflectivity: For homogeneous and semi-infinite materials, reflectivity is the same as reflectance.
criteria.q799: Refractive Index: "refractive index" or index of refraction n of a substance (optical medium) is a dimensionless number that describes how light, or any other radiation, propagates through that medium.
criteria.q800: Relative Atomic Mass: "Relative Atomic Mass " is a dimensionless physical quantity, the ratio of the average mass of atoms of an element (from a given source) to 1/12 of the mass of an atom of carbon-12 (known as the unified atomic mass unit)
criteria.q801: Relative Humidity: $\textit{Relative Humidity}$ is the ratio of the partial pressure of water vapour in an air-water mixture to the saturated vapour pressure of water at a prescribed temperature.
criteria.q802: Relative Mass Concentration of Vapour: Relative Mass Concentration of Vapour is one of a number of Relative Concentration quantities defined by ISO 80000.
criteria.q803: Relative Mass Defect: The "Relative Mass Defect" is the mass defect between the monoisotopic mass of an element and the mass of its A + 1 or its A + 2 isotopic cluster.
criteria.q804: Relative Mass Density: Relative density, or specific gravity, is the ratio of the density (mass of a unit volume) of a substance to the density of a given reference material.
criteria.q805: Relative Mass Excess: The "Relative Mass Excess" is the mass excess between the monoisotopic mass of an element and the mass of its A + 1 or its A + 2 isotopic cluster (extrapolated from relative mass defect).
criteria.q806: Relative Mass Ratio of Vapour: Relative Mass Ratio of Vapour is one of a number of Relative Concentration quantities defined by ISO 80000.
criteria.q807: Relative Molecular Mass: "Relative Molecular Mass " is equivalent to the numerical value of the molecular mass expressed in unified atomic mass units.
criteria.q808: Relative Partial Pressure: Relative Partial Pressure
criteria.q809: Relative Pressure Coefficient: Relative Pressure Coefficient
criteria.q810: Relaxation Time: "Relaxation Time" is a time constant for exponential decay towards equilibrium.
criteria.q811: Relaxation Time: "Relaxation Time" is a time constant for exponential decay towards equilibrium.
criteria.q812: Reluctance: "Reluctance" or magnetic resistance, is a concept used in the analysis of magnetic circuits.
criteria.q813: Residual Resistivity: "Residual Resistivity" for metals, is the resistivity extrapolated to zero thermodynamic temperature.
criteria.q814: Resistance: The electrical resistance of an object is a measure of its opposition to the passage of a steady electric current.
criteria.q816: Resistivity: "Resistivity" is the inverse of the conductivity when this inverse exists.
criteria.q817: Resonance Energy: "Resonance Energy" in a nuclear reaction, is the kinetic energy of an incident particle, in the reference frame of the target, corresponding to a resonance in a nuclear reaction.
criteria.q818: Resonance Escape Probability: The "Resonance Escape Probability" is the fraction of fission neutrons that manage to slow down from fission to thermal energies without being absorbed.
criteria.q819: Resonance Escape Probability for Fission: Fraction of fission neutrons that manage to slow down from fission to thermal energies without being absorbed.
criteria.q820: Respiratory Rate: Respiratory rate (Vf, Rf or RR) is also known by respiration rate, pulmonary ventilation rate, ventilation rate, or breathing frequency is the number of breaths taken within a set amount of time, typically 60 seconds.
criteria.q821: Rest Energy: "Rest Energy" is the energy equivalent of the rest mass of a body, equal to the rest mass multiplied by the speed of light squared.
criteria.q822: Rest Mass: The $\textit{Rest Mass}$, the invariant mass, intrinsic mass, proper mass, or (in the case of bound systems or objects observed in their center of momentum frame) simply mass, is a characteristic of the total energy and momentum of an objec
criteria.q823: Reverberation Time: Reverberation Time is the time required for reflections of a direct sound to decay by 60 dB below the level of the direct sound.
criteria.q824: Reynolds Number: The "Reynolds Number" (Re) is a dimensionless number that gives a measure of the ratio of inertial forces to viscous forces and consequently quantifies the relative importance of these two types of forces for given flow conditions.
criteria.q825: Richardson Constant: "Richardson Constant" is a constant used in developing thermionic emission current density for a metal.
criteria.q826: rotary-translatory motion conversion: rotary-translatory motion conversion
criteria.q827: Rotary-translatory Motion Conversion: Rotary-translatory Motion Conversion
criteria.q828: Rotational Frequency: IfcRotationalFrequencyMeasure is a measure of the number of cycles that an item revolves in unit time.
criteria.q829: Rotational Mass: "Rotational Mass" denotes the inertia of a body with respect to angular acceleration.
criteria.q830: Rotational Stiffness: Rotational Stiffness is the extent to which an object resists deformation in response to an applied torque.
criteria.q831: Rotational Frequency: IfcRotationalFrequencyMeasure is a measure of the number of cycles that an item revolves in unit time.

criteria.q832: Scalar Magnetic Potential: "Scalar Magnetic Potential" is the scalar potential of an irrotational magnetic field strength.
criteria.q833: Second Axial Moment of Area: The moment of inertia, also called mass moment of inertia, rotational inertia, polar moment of inertia of mass, or the angular mass is a property of a distribution of mass in space that measures its resistance to rotational acceleration abo
criteria.q834: Second Moment of Area: The second moment of area is a property of a physical object that can be used to predict its resistance to bending and deflection.
criteria.q835: Reaction Rate Constant: A quantity kind that is a proportionality constant that quantifies the relationship between the molar concentrations of the reactants and the rate of a second order chemical reaction.
criteria.q836: Second Polar Moment of Area: The moment of inertia, also called mass moment of inertia, rotational inertia, polar moment of inertia of mass, or the angular mass is a property of a distribution of mass in space that measures its resistance to rotational acceleration abo
criteria.q837: Section Area Integral: The sectional area integral measure is typically used in torsional analysis.
criteria.q838: Section Modulus: The Section Modulus is a geometric property for a given cross-section used in the design of beams or flexural members.
criteria.q839: Seebeck Coefficient: "Seebeck Coefficient", or thermopower, or thermoelectric power of a material is a measure of the magnitude of an induced thermoelectric voltage in response to a temperature difference across that material.
criteria.q840: Serum Level: Concentration of a biologically active substance in blood serum, expressed in International Units per volume (e.g.
criteria.q841: Serum or Plasma Level: Serum or Plasma Level
criteria.q842: Service Factor: The value indicates the multiplier of the rated power that equipment can handle for some period of time when operating according to a manufacturer's specified conditions; typically applicable to motors.
criteria.q843: Shannon Diversity Index: Information entropy applied to a collection of indiviual organisms [of selected species] in a sample area.
criteria.q844: Shear Modulus: The Shear Modulus or modulus of rigidity, denoted by $G$, or sometimes $S$ or $\mu$, is defined as the ratio of shear stress to the shear strain.
criteria.q845: Shear Strain: Shear Strain is the amount of deformation perpendicular to a given line rather than parallel to it.
criteria.q846: Shear Stress: Shear stress occurs when the force occurs in shear, or perpendicular to the normal.
criteria.q847: Short-Range Order Parameter: "Short-Range Order Parameter" is the fraction of the nearest-neighbor atom pairs in an Ising ferromagnet having magnetic moments in one direction, minus the fraction having magnetic moments in the opposite direction.
criteria.q848: Short-Range Order Parameter: "Short-Range Order Parameter" is the fraction of the nearest-neighbor atom pairs in an Ising ferromagnet having magnetic moments in one direction, minus the fraction having magnetic moments in the opposite direction.
criteria.q849: Signal Detection Threshold: "Signal Detection Threshold" is a dimensionless measure of the threshold for detecting a signal against a background of noise.
criteria.q850: Signal Strength: In telecommunications, particularly in radio, signal strength refers to the magnitude of the electric field at a reference point that is a significant distance from the transmitting antenna.
criteria.q851: Slowing-Down Area: "Slowing-Down Area" in an infinite homogenous medium, is one-sixth of the mean square distance between the neutron source and the point where a neutron reaches a given energy.
criteria.q852: Slowing-Down Density: "Slowing-Down Density" is a measure of the rate at which neutrons lose energy in a nuclear reactor through collisions; equal to the number of neutrons that fall below a given energy per unit volume per unit time.
criteria.q853: Slowing-Down Length: "Slowing-Down Length" is the average straight-line distance that a fast neutron will travel between its introduction into the slowing-downmedium (moderator) and thermalization.
criteria.q854: Slowing-Down Area: "Slowing-Down Area" in an infinite homogenous medium, is one-sixth of the mean square distance between the neutron source and the point where a neutron reaches a given energy.
criteria.q855: Slowing-Down Density: "Slowing-Down Density" is a measure of the rate at which neutrons lose energy in a nuclear reactor through collisions; equal to the number of neutrons that fall below a given energy per unit volume per unit time.
criteria.q856: Slowing-Down Length: "Slowing-Down Length" is the average straight-line distance that a fast neutron will travel between its introduction into the slowing-downmedium (moderator) and thermalization.
criteria.q857: Soil Adsorption Coefficient: A specific volume that is the ratio of the amount of substance adsorbed per unit weight of organic carbon in the soil or sediment to the concentration of the chemical in aqueous solution at equilibrium.
criteria.q858: Solid Angle: The solid angle subtended by a surface S is defined as the surface area of a unit sphere covered by the surface S's projection onto the sphere.
criteria.q859: Diffusion Length (Solid State Physics): "Solid State Diffusion Length" is the average distance traveled by a particle, such as a minority carrier in a semiconductor
criteria.q860: Water Solubility: An amount of substance per unit volume that is the concentration of a saturated solution expressed as the ratio of the solute concentration over the volume of water.
criteria.q861: Sound Energy Density: Sound energy density is the time-averaged sound energy in a given volume divided by that volume.
criteria.q862: Sound Exposure: Sound Exposure is the energy of the A-weighted sound calculated over the measurement time(s).
criteria.q863: Sound Exposure Level: Sound Exposure Level abbreviated as $SEL$ and $LAE$, is the total noise energy produced from a single noise event, expressed as a logarithmic ratio from a reference level.
criteria.q864: Sound Intensity: Sound intensity or acoustic intensity ($I$) is defined as the sound power $P_a$ per unit area $A$.
criteria.q865: Sound Particle Acceleration: In a compressible sound transmission medium - mainly air - air particles get an accelerated motion: the particle acceleration or sound acceleration with the symbol a in $m/s2$.
criteria.q866: Sound Particle Displacement: Sound Particle Displacement is the nstantaneous displacement of a particle in a medium from what would be its position in the absence of sound waves.
criteria.q867: Sound Particle Velocity: Sound Particle velocity is the velocity v of a particle (real or imagined) in a medium as it transmits a wave.
criteria.q868: Sound Power: Sound power or acoustic power $P_a$ is a measure of sonic energy $E$ per time $t$ unit.
criteria.q869: Sound Power Level: Sound Power Level abbreviated as $SWL$ expresses sound power more practically as a relation to the threshold of hearing - 1 picoW - in a logarithmic scale.
criteria.q870: Sound Pressure: Sound Pressure is the difference between instantaneous total pressure and static pressure.
criteria.q871: Sound Pressure Level: Sound pressure level ($SPL$) or sound level is a logarithmic measure of the effective sound pressure of a sound relative to a reference value.
criteria.q872: Sound Reduction Index: The Sound Reduction Index is used to measure the level of sound insulation provided by a structure such as a wall, window, door, or ventilator.
criteria.q873: Sound Volume Velocity: Sound Volume Velocity is the product of particle velocity $v$ and the surface area $S$ through which an acoustic wave of frequency $f$ propagates.
criteria.q874: Source Voltage: The quantity kind $\textit{Source Voltage}$, also referred to as $\textit{Source Tension}$ is the voltage between the two terminals of a voltage source when there is no electric current through the source.
criteria.q875: Source Voltage Between Substances: "Source Voltage Between Substances" is the source voltage between substance a and b.
criteria.q876: Spatial Summation Function: "Spatial Summation Function" is he ability to produce a composite signal from the signals coming into the eyes from different directions.
criteria.q877: Specific Acoustic Impedance: $\textit{Specific Acoustic Impedance}$ at a point in a medium is the complex quotient of the sound pressure $p$ by the particle velocity $v$ in the direction of wave propagation: $z = p / v$.
criteria.q878: Specific Activity: The "Specific Activity" is the number of decays per unit time of a radioactive sample.
criteria.q879: Specific Electric Charge: Electric charge (often capacity in the context of electrochemical cells) relativ to the mass (often only active components).
criteria.q880: Specific Electrical Current: "Specific Electric Current" is a measure to specify the applied current relative to a corresponding mass.
criteria.q881: Specific Energy: $\textit{Specific Energy}$ is defined as the energy per unit mass.
criteria.q882: Specific Energy Imparted: The "Specific Energy Imparted", is the energy imparted to an element of irradiated matter divided by the mass, dm, of that element.
criteria.q883: Specific Enthalpy: $\textit{Specific Enthalpy}$ is enthalpy per mass of substance involved.
criteria.q884: Specific Entropy: "Specific Entropy" is entropy per unit of mass.
criteria.q885: Specific Gibbs Energy: Energy has corresponding intensive (size-independent) properties for pure materials.
criteria.q886: Specific Heat Capacity: Specific Heat Capacity of a solid or liquid is defined as the heat required to raise unit mass of substance by one degree of temperature.
criteria.q887: Specific Heat Capacity at Constant Pressure: Specific heat at a constant pressure.
criteria.q888: Specific Heat Capacity at Constant Volume: Specific heat per constant volume.
criteria.q889: Specific Heat Capacity at Saturation: Specific heat per constant volume.
criteria.q890: Specific Heat Pressure: Specific heat at a constant pressure.
criteria.q891: Specific Heat Volume: Specific heat per constant volume.
criteria.q892: Specific Heats Ratio: The ratio of specific heats, for the exhaust gases adiabatic gas constant, is the relative amount of compression/expansion energy that goes into temperature $T$ versus pressure $P$ can be characterized by the heat capacity ratio: $\gamma\fr
criteria.q893: Specific Helmholtz Energy: $\textit{Specific Helmholtz Energy}$ is a "corresponding intensive property", which is $\textit{Helmholz Energy}$ per mass of substance involved.
criteria.q894: Specific Humidity: Specific humidity (or moisture content) is the ratio of the mass of water vapour to the total mass of the air parcel.
criteria.q895: Specific Impulse: The impulse produced by a rocket divided by the mass $mp$ of propellant consumed.

criteria.q896: Specific Impulse by Mass: Specific Impulse by Mass
criteria.q897: Specific Impulse by Weight: Specific impulse expressed on a weight basis: the impulse produced divided by the weight of propellant consumed, $I_{sp} = F / (\dot{m} g_0)$, giving a result in seconds.
criteria.q898: Specific Internal Energy: Energy has corresponding intensive (size-independent) properties for pure materials.
criteria.q899: Specific Modulus: Specific modulus is a materials property consisting of the elastic modulus per mass density of a material.
criteria.q900: Specific Optical Rotatory Power: The "Specific Optical Rotatory Power" Angle of optical rotation divided by the optical path length through the medium and by the mass concentration of the substance giving the specific optical rotatory power.
criteria.q901: Specific Power: Specific power, also known as power-to-weight ratio, is the amount of power output per unit mass of the power source.
criteria.q902: Specific Surface Area: Specific surface area (SSA) is a property of solids defined as the total surface area (SA) of a material per unit mass, (with units of m²/kg or m²/g).
criteria.q903: Specific Thrust: Specific impulse (usually abbreviated Isp) is a way to describe the efficiency of rocket and jet engines.
criteria.q904: Specific Volume: "Specific Volume" ($\nu$) is the volume occupied by a unit of mass of a material.
criteria.q905: Specific Weight: The specific weight, also known as the unit weight is a volume-specific quantity defined as the weight per unit volume of a material.
criteria.q906: Spectral Angular Cross-section: "Spectral Angular Cross-section" is the cross-section for ejecting or scattering a particle into an elementary cone with energy $E$ in an energy interval, divided by the solid angle $d\Omega$ of that cone and the range $dE$ of that interval
criteria.q907: Spectral Cross-section: "Spectral Cross-section" is the cross-section for a process in which the energy of the ejected or scattered particle is in an interval of energy, divided by the range $dE$ of this interval.
criteria.q908: Spectral Density of Vibrational Modes: The number of vibrational modes in an infinitesimal interval of angular frequency, divided by the size of that interval and by volume.
criteria.q909: Measurement Unit of Spectral Emittance: Spectral Emittance is a radiometry term for the power per unit area of electromagnetic radiation unit wavelength emerging from a surface.
criteria.q910: Measurement Unit of Spectral Irradiance: Spectral Irradiance is a radiometry term for the power per unit area of electromagnetic radiation per unit wavelength incident at a surface.
criteria.q911: Spectral Luminous Efficiency: The Spectral Luminous Efficiency is a measure of how well a light source produces visible light.
criteria.q912: Measurement Unit of Spectral Radiance: Spectral Radiance is a radiometry term for the power per unit area of electromagnetic radiation per unit wavelength per unit solid angle emerging from a surface.
criteria.q913: Spectral Radiant Energy Density: "Spectral Radiant Energy Density" is the spectral concentration of radiant energy density (in terms of wavelength), or the spectral radiant energy density (in terms of wave length).
criteria.q914: Spectral Radiant Energy Density in Terms of Wavelength: Spectral Radiant Energy Density in Terms of Wavelength
criteria.q915: Speed: Speed is the magnitude of velocity.
criteria.q916: Speed of Light: The quantity kind $\text{Speed of Light}$ is the speed of electomagnetic waves in a given medium.
criteria.q917: Speed of Sound: The speed of sound is the distance travelled during a unit of time by a sound wave propagating through an elastic medium.
criteria.q918: Speed Ratio: Speed ratio generally refers to the ratio of the rotational speeds of two interconnected rotating components, but it sometimes relates linear speeds.
criteria.q919: Illuminance: Spherical illuminance is equal to quotient of the total luminous flux $\Phi_v$ incident on a small sphere by the cross section area of that sphere.
criteria.q920: Spin: In quantum mechanics and particle physics "Spin" is an intrinsic form of angular momentum carried by elementary particles, composite particles (hadrons), and atomic nuclei.
criteria.q921: Spin Quantum Number: The "Spin Quantum Number" describes the spin (intrinsic angular momentum) of the electron within that orbital, and gives the projection of the spin angular momentum S along the specified axis
criteria.q924: Standard Absolute Activity: The "Standard Absolute Activity" is proportional to the absoulte activity of the pure substance $B$ at the same temperature and pressure multiplied by the standard pressure.
criteria.q925: Standard Chemical Potential: "Standard Chemical Potential" is the value of the chemical potential at standard conditions
criteria.q926: Standard Gravitational Parameter: In celestial mechanics the standard gravitational parameter of a celestial body is the product of the gravitational constant G and the mass M of the body.
criteria.q927: State Density as Expression of Angular Frequency: Quotient aus Anzahl von Vibrationsmodi in einem infinitesimalen Intervall der Kreisfrequenz durch die Spannweite dieses Intervalls und das Volumen
criteria.q928: State of Charge: ""State of Charge",quantifies the remaining capacity available in a battery at a given time and in relation to a given state of ageing.
criteria.q929: Static Friction: Static friction is friction between two or more solid objects that are not moving relative to each other.
criteria.q930: Static Friction Coefficient: Static friction is friction between two or more solid objects that are not moving relative to each other.
criteria.q931: Static Pressure: "Static Pressure" is the pressure at a nominated point in a fluid.
criteria.q932: Statistical Weight: A "Statistical Weight" is the relative probability (possibly unnormalized) of a particular feature of a state.
criteria.q933: Stochastic Process: In probability theory, a stochastic process, or sometimes random process is a collection of random variables; this is often used to represent the evolution of some random value, or system, over time.
criteria.q934: Stoichiometric Number: Chemical reactions, as macroscopic unit operations, consist of simply a very large number of elementary reactions, where a single molecule reacts with another molecule.
criteria.q935: Strain: In any branch of science dealing with materials and their behaviour, strain is the geometrical expression of deformation caused by the action of stress on a physical body.
criteria.q936: Strain Energy Density: Defined as the 'work done' for a given strain, that is the area under the stress-strain curve after a specified eation.
criteria.q937: Strain Energy Release Rate: In fracture mechanics, the energy release rate, G, is the rate at which energy is transformed as a material undergoes fracture.
criteria.q938: Stress: Stress is a measure of the average amount of force exerted per unit area of a surface within a deformable body on which internal forces act.
criteria.q939: Stress Intensity Factor: In fracture mechanics, the stress intensity factor (K) is used to predict the stress state ("stress intensity") near the tip of a crack or notch caused by a remote load or residual stresses.
criteria.q940: Stress-Optic Coefficient: When a ray of light passes through a photoelastic material, its electromagnetic wave components are resolved along the two principal stress directions and each component experiences a different refractive index due to the birefringence.
criteria.q941: Structural Efficiency: Structural efficiency is a function of the weight of structure to the afforded vehicle's strength.
criteria.q942: Structure Factor: "Structure Factor" is a mathematical description of how a material scatters incident radiation.
criteria.q943: Sun Protection Factor of a Product: Sun Protection Factor of a Product
criteria.q944: Superconduction Transition Temperature: "Superconduction Transition Temperature" is the critical thermodynamic temperature of a superconductor.
criteria.q945: Superconductor Energy Gap: "Superconductor Energy Gap" is the width of the forbidden energy band in a superconductor.
criteria.q946: Surface Activity Density: The "Surface Activity Density" is undefined.
criteria.q947: Surface Coefficient of Heat Transfer: Surface Coefficient of Heat Transfer
criteria.q948: Surface Density: The area density (also known as areal density, surface density, or superficial density) of a two-dimensional object is calculated as the mass per unit area.
criteria.q949: Surface‑related Volume Flow Rate: Surface‑related Volume Flow Rate
criteria.q950: Surface Tension: "Surface Tension" is a contractive tendency of the surface of a liquid that allows it to resist an external force.
criteria.q951: Susceptance: "Susceptance" is the imaginary part of admittance.
criteria.q952: Systolic Blood Pressure: The pressure of blood in the arteries which rises to a maximum as blood is pumped out by the left ventricle (systole) and drops to a minimum in diastole.
criteria.q953: Target Bogie Mass: An informal mass limit established by a Project Office (at the Element Integrated Product Team (IPT) level or below) to control mass.
criteria.q954: Temperature: Temperature is a physical property of matter that quantitatively expresses the common notions of hot and cold.
criteria.q955: Temperature Amount of Substance: Temperature Amount of Substance
criteria.q956: Temperature Difference: Temperature difference (Delta T) is the difference of temperatures between two measuring points
criteria.q957: Temperature Gradient: The temperature gradient measures the difference of a temperature per length, as for instance used in an external wall or its layers.
criteria.q958: Temperature per Magnetic Flux Density: Temperature per Magnetic Flux Density
criteria.q959: Temperature per Square Time: Temperature per Square Time

criteria.q960: Temperature per Time: Temperature per Time
criteria.q961: Temperature per Time Squared: Temperature per Time Squared
criteria.q962: Temperature Rate of Change: The "Temperature Rate of Change" measures the difference of a temperature per time (positive: rise, negative: fall), as for instance used with heat sensors.
criteria.q964: Temperature Variance: Variance for temperature data.
criteria.q965: Temperature Variance, NEON: Variance for NEON temperature data measured in degrees celcius
criteria.q966: Temporal Summation Function: "Temporal Summation Function" is the ability of the human eye to produce a composite signal from the signals coming into an eye during a short time interval.
criteria.q968: Thermal Admittance: The heat transfer coefficient is also known as thermal admittance in the sense that the material may be seen as admitting heat to flow.
criteria.q969: Thermal Conductance: This quantity is also called "Heat Transfer Coefficient".
criteria.q970: Thermal Conductivity: In physics, thermal conductivity, $k$ (also denoted as $\lambda$), is the property of a material's ability to conduct heat.
criteria.q971: Thermal Diffusion Factor: Thermal diffusion is a phenomenon in which a temperature gradient in a mixture of fluids gives rise to a flow of one constituent relative to the mixture as a whole.
criteria.q972: Thermal Diffusion Ratio: The "Thermal Diffusion Ratio" is proportional to the product of the component concentrations.
criteria.q973: Thermal Diffusion Coefficient: Thermal Diffusion Coefficient
criteria.q974: Thermal Diffusivity: In heat transfer analysis, thermal diffusivity (usually denoted $\alpha$ but $a$, $\kappa$,$k$, and $D$ are also used) is the thermal conductivity divided by density and specific heat capacity at constant pressure.

property.definition: Viscosity is a measure of the resistance of a fluid which is being deformed by either shear stress or extensional stress.
property.fullDefinition: Viscosity is a measure of the resistance of a fluid which is being deformed by either shear stress or extensional stress. In general terms it is the resistance of a liquid to flow, or its "thickness". Viscosity describes a fluid's internal resistance to flow and may be thought of as a measure of fluid friction. [Wikipedia]. In general conversation or in non-scientific contexts, if someone refers to the viscosity of a fluid, they're likely talking about its dynamic (or absolute) viscosity. However, in engineering or scientific contexts, it's essential to clarify which type of viscosity is being discussed, as the interpretation and use of the data may differ depending on whether one is talking about dynamic or kinematic viscosity.

property.definition: The mass density or density of a material is defined as its mass per unit volume.
property.fullDefinition: The mass density or density of a material is defined as its mass per unit volume. The symbol most often used for density is $\rho$. Mathematically, density is defined as mass divided by volume: $\rho = m/V$, where $\rho$ is the density, $m$ is the mass, and $V$ is the volume. In some cases, density is also defined as its weight per unit volume, although this quantity is more properly called specific weight.

property.definition: The mass density or density of a material is defined as its mass per unit volume.
property.fullDefinition: The mass density or density of a material is defined as its mass per unit volume. The symbol most often used for density is $\rho$. Mathematically, density is defined as mass divided by volume: $\rho = m/V$, where $\rho$ is the density, $m$ is the mass, and $V$ is the volume. In some cases, density is also defined as its weight per unit volume, although this quantity is more properly called specific weight.
